key_insight: AegisDx reframes AI diagnosis as a safety-first reasoning workflow, using structured checks to broaden differentials and explicitly guard against missing dangerous conditions.
clinical_relevance: For acute care decision support, this approach may be more useful than single-shot prediction because it improves identification of high-risk diagnoses and produces more transparent, evidence-grounded next steps.
method: Coordinates multiple LLM roles with role-specific contracts
Uses structured intermediate outputs, evidence retrieval, and verification gates
evidence_signal: Across literature cases and real emergency department notes, AegisDx improved top-3 diagnostic performance and physician-rated safety, including higher capture of must-not-miss diagnoses and better composite safety scores.
watch_item: Results come from specific benchmark cases and a blinded physician review, so real-world impact, workflow fit, and safety under broader deployment still need prospective validation.
paper_title: A safety-oriented hypothetico-deductive framework for AI-assisted differential diagnosis
